Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2014/03/essay-how-weigh-everything-atoms-apples-using-revised-si UPDATES Essay: How to Weigh Everything from Atoms to Apples Using the Revised SI March 26, 2014 Share Facebook Linkedin X.com Email New NIST watt balance, open for assembly and testing. In its final operating configuration, it will be covered and operate in vacuum. Very soon, the International System of Units (SI) may be revised to define the unit of mass in terms of a fixed value of the Planck constant, h . That move would end more than two centuries of dependence on an artifact standard kilogram that is very difficult to transfer and the mass of which drifts over time. It is not immediately obvious how mass is related to h , which is the constant used to determine the energy of a quantum mechanical entity such as a particle or wave. It is perhaps most familiar in the context of light, in the formulation E = hν, where E is energy (in joules) and ν is frequency. Mass, of course, does not appear explicitly in that equation, nor in the currently accepted value of the Planck constant: 6.62606X × 10 −34 joule second (J·s), where X is the final digit to be determined. Taxes must be paid as you earn or receive income during the year, either through withholding or estimated tax payments. If the amount of income tax withheld from your salary or pension is not enough, or if you receive income such as interest, dividends, alimony, self-employment income, capital gains, prizes and awards, you may have to make estimated tax payments. If you are in business for yourself, you generally need to make estimated tax payments. If you don’t pay enough tax through withholding and estimated tax payments, you may have to pay a penalty. March 19, 2025 Estimates: Burden of Foodborne Illness in the United States What to know Foodborne illness estimates can serve as a foundation for future public health action. CDC estimated the average number of U.S. foodborne illnesses, hospitalizations, and deaths in 2019 caused by seven major pathogens. Six of these pathogens caused 9.9 million domestically acquired foodborne illnesses. Illnesses caused by all seven pathogens resulted in 53,300 hospitalizations and 931 deaths. Why do we estimate? Knowing how many foodborne illnesses occur – or the burden of disease – provides us with a better understanding of an important public health problem. Surveillance systems and surveys provide vital information about the burden of foodborne illness in the United States, but they do not capture every illness. pages.description: Estonia is the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine.
pages.text: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes as backlash intensifies - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Estonia shares a border with Russia By Dan Roan Sports editor Published 13 November 2026 Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine. It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements. The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus. In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality". They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military. Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms. However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. It said a ban issued in 2022 will be maintained. In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation. pages.description: Este estudio investiga las disparidades laborales y salariales entre las personas con y sin discapacidad.
pages.text: Estudio sobre los resultados laborales y salariales de las personas con discapacidad | International Labour Organization Ir al contenido principal Documento de trabajo 124 Estudio sobre los resultados laborales y salariales de las personas con discapacidad Este estudio investiga las disparidades laborales y salariales entre las personas con y sin discapacidad. Facebook X Linkedin Detalles de la publicación Fecha 27 de agosto de 2024 Archivos para descargar PDF 2.5 MB Contenido también disponible en: English Este estudio investiga las disparidades laborales y salariales entre las personas con y sin discapacidad. Demuestra que las personas con discapacidad tienen menos probabilidades de participar en el mercado laboral y que, cuando lo hacen, se enfrentan a tasas de desempleo más elevadas, tienen más probabilidades de trabajar por cuenta propia y tienden a ganar salarios más bajos. Estas disparidades no parecen explicarse únicamente por características individuales como el nivel de estudios, la experiencia o la categoría profesional. Lo más probable es que se deban también a otros factores, como la escasez de adaptaciones en el lugar de trabajo en muchas empresas, la flexibilidad laboral potencialmente mayor que ofrece el trabajo por cuenta propia y la discriminación de las personas con discapacidad. En su última sección, el estudio destaca los marcos jurídicos establecidos a escala internacional y nacional para promover la igualdad de oportunidades y una remuneración justa para las personas con discapacidad. It provides confidential advice and guidance on professional ethics standards and dilemmas, specifically in relation to conflicts of interest. Its work is generally preventive and it supports the Organization for instance by providing training and capacity building to personnel, to enhance their abilities to do the right thing - also when no one is looking. While responsibility for ethical conduct lies with all members of FAO personnel, the Ethics Office supports personnel to navigate complex ethics and integrity issues, and help them interpret the rules that apply to them. The Ethics Office also promotes a workplace culture where individuals feel able to speak up without fear of retaliation. The FAO Oversight Advisory Committee provides guidance to the Ethics Office and assists with ensuring the ongoing quality of the performance of its functions. The OSI has been engaged with European policymakers over the past two years to ensure those laws don’t inadvertently harm Open Source. For Open Source developers, maintainers, and organizations, these developments raise important questions about how new regulatory frameworks apply across the software ecosystem. Clear, practical information is essential to help the community understand new requirements, distinguish applicable obligations, and continue building and sharing open technologies. The first milestone comes in the form of Commission guidance on the Cyber Resilience Act. The law establishes cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements, including vulnerability handling, security updates, and lifecycle responsibilities. pages.text: Eugène Delacroix (1798 - 1863) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Delacroix was the leading exponent of Romanticism in French painting. He was trained by the Neo-classical painter Pierre Guérin, from 1816 to about 1823. Guérin also taught Géricault . Delacroix first exhibited at the Salon in 1822. In style his work shows the influence of painters he had studied, notably Rubens . He was an admirer of English painting, and visited England in 1825. In 1832 he travelled to Spain, Morocco and Algiers. After the Revolution of 1830 he was favoured by Louis-Philippe, and later by Napoleon III, with a long series of official commissions, beginning in 1833 with a series of decorations in the Palais Bourbon. Delacroix exhibited at the Salon for the last time in 1859, showing Ovid among the Scythians . pages.text: Eugène Delacroix | Louis-Auguste Schwiter | NG3286 | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Eugène Delacroix, 'Louis-Auguste Schwiter', 1826-30 Louis-Auguste Schwiter Eugène Delacroix Central Hall Framed About the work Overview In-depth Overview Delacroix painted this portrait of fellow artist, Louis-Auguste Schwiter (1805–1899), in the early years of their lifelong friendship. Not only was this Delacroix’s first full-length portrait, but it also reveals the close attention he paid to work by British artists such as Thomas Gainsborough (1727–1788) and Thomas Lawrence (1769–1830). These portraits marked a departure from a more formal, heroic style of portraiture whose primary function was often the display of wealth and social status. The use of outdoor locations, such as parks and woodlands, was an important aspect of this new portraiture and Delacroix makes effective use of the dark sky and foliage to highlight areas of bright colour and, perhaps, to hint at Schwiter’s personality. Delacroix submitted the portrait to the Salon of 1827, but it was rejected. It was later bought by Edgar Degas (1834–1917) for his own collection. In-depth Louis-Auguste Schwiter (1805–1899) was an artist who exhibited regularly at the Paris Salon from 1831. He later inherited the title of baron. His friendship with Delacroix, seven years his senior and under whom he may have trained, lasted until Delacroix’s death in 1863. pages.text: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave 17 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Matthew Kenyon Technology reporter, The Hague AFP via Getty Images Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO. If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger. The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical. They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre). Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips. Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s. "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." pages.text: Europe's best multi-day hikes you can do without camping | National Geographic TRAVEL Europe's best multi-day hikes you can do without camping A long-distance trek is challenging enough, without having to pitch a tent every night. Here’s our pick of the continent’s most rewarding routes, complete with atmospheric overnight stays. There's plenty of long-distance hiking in various terrains available in Europe. Westend61, Getty Images By Sean Newsom Published June 10, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). A multi-day hike is a very particular kind of challenge. The demands on mind and body layer up day after day and, to confront them in the best possible shape, it’s important to get proper rest each night. This is more easily done with a roof over your head than the flapping canvas of a tent and, in some protected landscapes, wild camping is forbidden. Happily, Europe is well-equipped with mountain refuges, pilgrim hostels and path-adjacent hotels. Many stand-out stays are in the Alps — but, as you’ll see from our guide, not all. South West Coast Path, England From a distance, it looks like madness — a whopping 630 miles of rollercoaster beach and cliff-top walking that wiggles through some of England’s most popular seaside destinations. But the closer you get, the more enticing the South West Coast Path becomes — especially in Cornwall. Here lie the tallest cliffs and the most unspoilt landscapes, as well as deep layers of culture and history. pages.text: Europe's whale-watching season is starting. Here's where to see them | National Geographic TRAVEL Europe's whale-watching season is starting. Here's where to see them We round up five destinations where sightings of cetacean life are almost guaranteed in the spring and summer months, from hotspots off the Azores coast to the skerries between Scottish islands . Europe's waters are home to a variety of whale species, including sperm whales and humpback whales. Andrea Quartarone, Getty Images By James Stewart Published April 30, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Wildlife encounters don’t come much bigger than those with a whale. Coming face to fin with some of the largest mammals on the planet can be a deeply moving experience, one that’s become bucket list for many travellers. Since commercial whale-watching began around 70 years ago, it’s grown into a worldwide industry worth an estimated £1bn. An increasing number of countries are drawing up regulations that put nature first, but it’s still key to choose operators that prioritise animal welfare over close-up encounters. Húsavík, Iceland Come to the north coast of Iceland in early summer for minkes, humpbacks, huge pods of orcas and various dolphins — plus, Europe’s highest chances of spotting blue whales. You’re almost guaranteed a sighting of something between June and September, when krill are plentiful in the high latitudes and long days extend viewing opportunities. pages.text: European T20 Premier League: board director Warren Deutrom says ETPL will definitely return in 2027 but earlier in the summer after poor attendances in Ireland - BBC Sport Image source, ETPL Image caption, Mitchell Santner captained Edinburgh Rockers to victory in the ETPL final By Timothy Abraham BBC Sport Journalist Published 22 September 2026 The European T20 Premier League will definitely be back in 2027 but is set to be shifted to earlier in the summer in a bid to boost attendances, says tournament board director Warren Deutrom. Matches during the group stage in Ireland were played out in a sparsely-populated Malahide, even when admission was free for certain games. Edinburgh Castle Rockers beat Belfast Wolves by seven wickets to win the inaugural edition of the ETPL on Sunday in front of a larger crowd, but a number of the temporary seats were still vacant. Crowds for the Dutch leg of the inaugural tournament in Voorburg were healthier, albeit in a much smaller venue. Deutrom said the ETPL are already taking steps to move the tournament to a time of the year to coincide with the school holidays to help get more fans through the gates. "I'm not worried about trying things in year one and if it wasn't successful, then we learn for year two," he told BBC Sport. "One of the learnings would be in terms of window, and we are actively looking at an earlier slot, probably more likely July next year. Photograph: Nick Suydam/Alamy Illinois Evacuation zone lifted after bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating Ramon Antonio Vargas Sat 14 Nov 2026 15.14 EST First published on Sat 14 Nov 2026 09.13 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol production plant. The discovery reported at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria triggered a mandatory evacuation over a one-mile evacuation zone encompassing sections of that city as well as the adjacent municipality of East Peoria. Officials ultimately lifted the evacuation zone at about 1.25pm local time on Saturday – but only after making it clear there had genuinely been a bomb found and ruling out the presence of any other explosives. “It is real – this is a real thing,” Peoria’s mayor, Rita Ali, initially said , according to local news outlet WMBD. “We know that is a real threat. pages.description: This evaluation examines a health system strengthening programme, focusing on the treatment of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) and Diabetes Mellitus (DM).
pages.text: Evaluation of CL and DM Programs in Syria | ICRC Skip to main content Report 16-03-2026 2 languages English 中文 Syria: Evaluation of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis and Diabetes Mellitus Programs Syria Evaluations at the ICRC: Evidence-based learning Health This evaluation examines a health system strengthening programme implemented in partnership with Syria’s Ministry of Health (MoH), focusing on the treatment of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) and Diabetes Mellitus (DM). It assessed programme achievements and identified opportunities for sustainable knowledge transfer and handover to national authorities. Diman Ameen/ICRC Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Findings indicate that sustainability considerations were incorporated into programme design, though their implementation varied across locations depending on service modality and operational conditions. Service delivery expanded significantly, with the number of treated CL and DM cases more than doubling since 2018. However, community feedback mechanisms remained largely informal. The programme maintained relevance through adaptive design and coordination with national health authorities and partners. At the same time, monitoring systems could be further strengthened to better capture partnership contributions and longer-term health system strengthening effects. Further details are provided in the executive summary. pages.title: Evaluation of EcoSec’s Microeconomic Initiatives in Libya 2019-2024 | ICRC
pages.description: The purpose of the evaluation was to assess the effectiveness, relevance, and impact of Microeconomic Initiatives (MEIs) implemented by EcoSec in Libya between 2019-2024.
pages.text: Evaluation of EcoSec’s Microeconomic Initiatives in Libya 2019-2024 | ICRC Skip to main content Report 25-08-2026 Evaluation of EcoSec’s Microeconomic Initiatives in Libya 2019-2024 Libya Evaluations at the ICRC: Evidence-based learning Economic Security The purpose of the evaluation was to assess the effectiveness, relevance, and impact of Microeconomic Initiatives (MEIs) implemented by EcoSec in Libya between 2019-2024. The primary objective of an MEI is to provide its beneficiaries with an income that supports them to meet their household’s basic needs from its own resources. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook The evaluation addressed seven key evaluation questions organized by relevance, effectiveness, and impact OECD-DAC criteria, as well as cross-cutting themes relating to program monitoring and AAP. The evaluation found out that MEIs are relevant to the specific needs of conflict-affected households in Libya. Specifically, MEIs are responsive to needs for access to sustainable livelihoods and stable income generation. Besides, despite gaps in ICRC organizational processes, the program produces benefits in the short term along sustainable and resilient livelihood pathways. Five recommendations have been submitted for this evaluation. This includes addressing the technical challenges in MEI programming within current parameters (multi-year planning, market assessments, beneficiary selection, grant amount, additional training), setting clearer expectations for MEI program results. pages.description: The purpose of this evaluation was to identify programme's effectiveness and the continued relevance of EcoSec interventions implemented in Cameroon from 2019 to 2024.
pages.text: Evaluation of the ICRC’s EcoSec Programme in Cameroon (2019-2024) | ICRC Skip to main content Report 25-08-2026 Evaluation of the ICRC’s EcoSec Programme in Cameroon (2019-2024) Cameroon Evaluations at the ICRC: Evidence-based learning Economic Security The purpose of this evaluation was to identify programme's effectiveness and the continued relevance of EcoSec interventions implemented in Cameroon from 2019 to 2024. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook The evaluation found that the objectives of the EcoSec programme are closely aligned with the needs of targeted populations. This is true even as these needs vary sharply, depending on the region covered. The scale of needs far exceeds the capacity of the programme, which makes prioritisation especially critical. The three main pillars of the EcoSec programme form a coherent range of activities. This is true even as these activities are often conducted independently of each other, and do not always contribute to the same geographically circumscribed outcomes. Given the strong diversity of environments in which it operates, the ability of the programme to achieve a broad range of differentiated outcomes is an asset, as it enables the programme to be adaptive and context appropriate. In both the Far North and NWSW, there is strong evidence that the EcoSec programme has markedly and meaningfully improved conditions for the target population. The policy represents a commitment to conducting rigorous, relevant evaluations and to using evidence from evaluations to inform policy and practice. DOL seeks to promote rigor, relevance, transparency, independence, and ethics in the conduct of evaluations. This policy addresses each of these principles. The mission of the Department of Labor is to "...foster, promote, and develop the welfare of the wage earners, job seekers, and retirees of the United States; improve working conditions; advance opportunities for profitable employment; and assure work-related benefits and rights." The importance of these goals demands that we continually innovate and improve, and that we evaluate the performance and effectiveness of our programs and activities. Through evaluation, DOL can learn systematically so that we can make our services as effective as possible. Evaluation produces one type of evidence. A learning organization with a culture of continual improvement requires many types of evidence, including not only evaluation but also descriptive research studies, performance measurement, financial and cost data, survey statistics, and program administrative data. Domanski David A. Yashar Other Contributors Janusz Wojtusiak, GMU EVAP-COND is a software package featuring NIST's simulation models EVAP and COND for finned-tube evaporators and condensers. The ‘tube-by-tube’ scheme in these simulation models allows for specifying complex refrigerant circuits, modeling refrigerant distribution between these circuits, and accounting for non-uniform air distribution. Simulation results provide local parameters for each tube, including refrigerant inlet and outlet quality, temperature, enthalpy, entropy, pressure drop, mass flow rate, and inlet and outlet air temperatures. EVAP-COND includes a module for optimization of refrigerant circuitry using computational intelligence methods. pages.text: Event | Making AI Work in Europe and Central Asia Apple Calendar Google Calendar Outlook Calendar Yahoo Calendar Outlook.com Calendar Office 365 Calendar Share Overview Speakers Growth in Europe and Central Asia is slowing, with higher energy import costs, persistent uncertainty, and slower growth in the European Union weighing on the outlook. By Joe Yogerst Last updated March 27, 2026 • 15 min read The 19th-century pioneers of Wayne County described Capitol Reef as “a bad place to lose a cow.” Fast forward more than a century and Utah's most underrated national park is a great place for visitors to lose themselves in nature. Capitol Reef is unique, starting with the fact that it rarely feels crowded. On any given day, you might be the only person hiking a particular trail or gazing down from an awesome viewpoint. Because Utah Highway 24 cuts across the middle of Capitol Reef, it’s one of the few national parks that visitors can sample without paying an entrance fee. Last but not least, this park is like a microcosm of other (more famous) Utah parks. It’s got soaring stone arches and towering red rock cliffs, narrow slot canyons and a lush river corridor, an array of typical Southwest wildlife—all built on the park’s rich history. Barnes Last updated July 14, 2026 • 20 min read Spanning an impressive 3.4 million acres across California and Nevada , Death Valley National Park is the largest national park in the lower 48 states, approximately the size of Connecticut . Though its name can be off-putting and it’s known as the driest, hottest, and lowest national park in the U.S., Death Valley is an interesting and diverse landscape that’s home to wildlife, wildflowers, and centuries of human history. Long before it became a national park, the land that comprises Death Valley was home to the Timbisha Shoshone people, who lived here for more than 1,000 years. They found everything they needed to survive on the land, from hunting to harvesting pinyon pine nuts and mesquite beans. In the second half of the 1800s, those heading west to California to seek their fortune came upon Death Valley; mining towns and borax factories popped up. One of those companies, the Pacific Coast Borax Company, saw the potential of tourism in Death Valley and began campaigning to have the area designated as a national park in the mid-1920s. pages.text: Everything you should know about Grand Canyon National Park | National Geographic By Joe Yogerst Last updated February 11, 2026 “Leave it as it is,” declared U.S. President Teddy Roosevelt after a 1903 sojourn at the Grand Canyon. “You cannot improve on it. The ages have been at work on it, and man can only mar it.” More than a century later, Arizona ’s “Big Ditch” continues to awe first-time visitors and those who've already been there a dozen times. Not so much from sheer size—although the dimensions are truly astounding—but an incredible combination of colors, shapes, weather, and wildlife. How grand is it? The massive gash in the Earth’s surface stretches 277 miles from east to west, measures 18 miles across at its widest point, and plunges around one mile from the rim to the Colorado River . As the elevation descends, the park transitions from pristine evergreen forest to stark desert landscapes with 1.8 billion years of geology. Native Americans have lived in and around the canyon for at least 12,000 years and Spanish explorers laid eyes upon the rift in the 16th century. But it wasn't until 1869 when John Wesley Powell and his team navigated the Colorado River through the canyon that it began to earn worldwide fame. Fast forward to today when more than six million people a year visit Grand Canyon National Park to experience its incredible vistas, hiking trails, historic hotels, and more. pages.text: Everything you should know about Lake District, the U.K.'s largest national park | National Geographic By Lynne Maxwell Published April 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). It’s no surprise that William Wordsworth took inspiration from this beautiful, 912sq-mile national park, packed with glistening lakes, rugged fells and some of the most epic views in the world. The English poet spent nine years living in Dove Cottage in Grasmere, a village now famed for its delectable gingerbread. Wordsworth wrote many of his best-loved poems during this time in the early 1800s, including the renowned I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud , and called the historic village “the loveliest spot that man hath ever found”. Children’s author Beatrix Potter was similarly besotted with the area, and her work was influenced by her idyllic childhood summers here in the 1880s. But the biggest draw for the 18 million people who visit The Lakes, as the area is colloquially known, every year is its dramatic mountain range and iconic fells, including England’s highest peak, Scafell Pike. The peak was popularised alongside 213 other rocky summits by Alfred Wainwright, the legendary fell-walker and author of The Pictorial Guides to the Lakeland Fells ; walkers can often be heard rejoicing at the achievement of ticking off ‘another Wainwright’. pages.text: Everything you should know about Plitvice Lakes National Park | National Geographic TRAVEL Everything you should know about Plitvice Lakes National Park Plitvice Lakes is Croatia’s oldest national park and one of its most extraordinary landscapes — breathtakingly beautiful and completely different from the Adriatic coast. Here’s how to explore it. Plitvice Lakes National Park covers an area of 115sq miles and was declared a Unesco World Heritage Site in 1979. Clement Leonard, Getty Images By Rudolf Abraham Last updated May 23, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Plitvice Lakes National Park is an exquisitely beautiful series of 16 lakes and myriad waterfalls, hemmed in by cliffs and surrounded by a vast area of forest, in Croatia’s Lika region. Together they form an ever-shifting watery landscape, turquoise and festooned with lush green mosses. What makes these lakes particularly special is that they’re separated by tufa barriers. Tufa is a porous rock, created over thousands of years by the precipitation of calcium carbonate from the water and its gradual deposition on mosses and other plants. The barriers are between six and seven thousand years old and are still forming. Designated a national park in 1949 (Nacionalni park Plitvička jezera) and covering an area of 115sq miles, it was declared a Unesco World Heritage Site in 1979, and in 1997 the Unesco-listed area was extended to match that of the national park. For the best paddleboarding, visitors at Voyageurs National Park should head to the sheltered bays of the four major interconnected lakes: Rainy, Kabetogama, Namakan, and Sandy Point. Per Breiehagen, Getty Images By Miles Griffis Last updated May 12, 2026 • 14 min read Hugging the Canadian border, Minnesota’s Voyageurs National Park is a floating landscape of glacially carved lakes fringed with thick boreal forests. The park was named for the French Canadian fur traders who paddled enormous birch and cedar canoes through the region in the 1800s. Today, “Voyageurs [National Park] offers you a view to the past to see the natural shoreline of this amazing lake country,” says Christina Hausman Rhode, the executive director of the nonprofit Voyageurs Conservancy . Though the park commemorates these hardy woodsmen, the region’s first stewards were the ancestors of the Bois Forte Chippewa (Ojibwe), who entered the area more than 10,000 years ago. They first paddled the three stately lakes—Kabetogama, Rainy, and Namakan—that circle the remote Kabetogama Peninsula, where packs of eastern gray wolves thrive.
